request.label: merge 2026w2
request.system:
You merge feature candidates extracted from the videos of a Microsoft Business Central launch event into one de-duplicated feature list.
Rules:
- Two candidates are the same feature when they describe the same capability or change, even under different names (e.g. "Copilot chat" and "Microsoft Copilot Chat in Business Central"). A product (the Expense Agent, the MCP server) is not one feature; its individual capabilities are. Keep features at the granularity a developer or consultant would search for.
- Do not invent features, do not drop candidates. Every candidate id appears in exactly one group.
- Use only the candidate texts. No outside product knowledge.
- Names: short, product-like, as the presenters say them, no marketing adjectives. Slugs: lowercase, hyphenated, stable, 2 to 6 words.
- No em-dashes anywhere. Use a plain hyphen.
request.prompt:
Wave: 2026w2. Area taxonomy: finance, supply-chain, e-documents, sustainability, expense-agent, copilot-and-agents, reporting-and-analytics, developer-tools, admin-and-platform, integration.
Below are 32 feature candidates, pre-grouped into 32 clusters by name similarity. A cluster is a hint, not a decision: split a cluster whose members are different things, merge clusters that are the same thing.
For each final group return: slug, name, area (one slug), dev_relevance (high if an AL developer must act or will use it, medium if it changes what they can build or test, low otherwise), 2 to 6 tags (lowercase), a 2 to 3 sentence summary written from the member descriptions only, and members (all candidate ids in the group).

groups.name: Page scripting generally available
groups.summary: The page scripting tool moves from preview to general availability in this release. It records and replays user actions in the web client, for example for user acceptance tests.

groups.name: Page scripting localization
groups.summary: Every user-facing string in page scripting is translated, including all steps, error messages, tooltips and previously hard-coded strings. This makes the tool ready for production use across all languages.

groups.name: Page scripting accessibility and usability pass
groups.summary: A pass on accessibility and usability was made to page scripting. Look and feel was also changed based on feedback.

groups.name: Multiple selection in grids (page scripting)
groups.summary: Page scripting recordings can now capture selecting several rows in a list and running bulk actions on them. Those steps can also be replayed.

groups.name: Validate message and error dialog text
groups.summary: A page scripting recording can now validate the text shown in a message or error dialog. This turns the recording into a real assertion instead of only a sequence of clicks.

groups.name: Agents generating page scripts
groups.summary: Since page scripting launched, agents can be used to try to generate page scripts and run them.

groups.name: AL MCP symbol search with source = environment
groups.summary: The AL MCP server can now search the connected environment, tell which app owns each object (with app version), and work with workspace and projects. The symbol search tool has a new source parameter that can be set to environment, so symbols are looked up on the remote server without downloading symbols or setting up dependencies first. Demoed by finding Customer Ledger Entry in the base app of the sandbox.

groups.name: Get next object ID tool (MCP)
groups.summary: A new MCP tool reads the app.json of the current project, works out the defined ID ranges and suggests free object IDs. In the demo it suggested free IDs in the 50,1xx range around the ones already used.

groups.name: AL language server (LSP)
groups.summary: A new standalone AL language server gives project-aware language intelligence over the language server protocol, so it is no longer tied to Visual Studio Code. In the demo, Copilot used go to definition and find references through it to explain how a fee calculation is used.

groups.name: Default implementation for interface methods
groups.summary: Interface methods can now have a default implementation, so consumers do not have to implement newly added methods. This lets interfaces grow over many releases without breaking existing implementers. A consumer sees a warning that a default exists and can still implement its own logic.

groups.name: Required pending attribute
groups.summary: Together with default implementations, an attribute lets the interface author tell consumers that implementing a new method will become mandatory later, for example in the next major or two. Consumers get a warning with a mandatory message instead of a break.

groups.name: Public package resources
groups.summary: Resources stored in an app can be shared across app boundaries by marking resource folders as public. Other apps can list apps with public resources, list resources per app ID and get them as JSON or text by passing the provider app ID, without a dependency. Private resources still work with the normal functions without an app ID.

groups.name: Integer to big integer field change
groups.summary: A field type can be changed from integer to big integer while keeping existing rows, aimed at ledger or sequence entries that run out of numbers. The compiler, AppSourceCop and the comparison with the previous app version show warnings such as implicit conversion and possible runtime overflow, but the change is allowed without copying data or a parallel implementation.

groups.name: Keys spanning base and extension fields
groups.summary: Table extensions are now merged into the base table, so a key can span both base table and table extension fields at the same time. Described as a long requested addition, it gives useful indexes for reading data by extension fields.

groups.name: Namespaces in translation IDs
groups.summary: XLIFF translation files can now be generated with fully qualified names, including the namespace, as ids instead of hash keys built from the name. This avoids collisions between objects with the same name in different namespaces and makes the ids readable.

groups.name: Action inherits page tooltip
groups.summary: An action that uses RunObject no longer needs its own tooltip, because the tooltip comes from the target page. The description is kept in one place and reused across many pages.

groups.name: Created by and modified by full name system fields
groups.summary: New system fields on the record hold the created by and modified by full names next to the user ids. They can be placed on pages in code and are customizable through personalization or customization, which was hard before because they were only rendered in the client.

groups.name: IsDirty on Record and RecordRef
groups.summary: A new IsDirty method on Record and RecordRef tests whether a record has changed. It lets you ask the user whether to save instead of comparing fields by hand.

groups.name: Explicit read isolation for isolated storage
groups.summary: Read isolation is now an explicit option when reading from isolated storage, for example read committed with an update lock instead of leaving it implied. It was only mentioned briefly in the summary.

groups.name: Data-driven tests (test data source)
groups.summary: One test method can run many scenarios taken from a data test source that lists test cases, such as overdue, not overdue and rounding. The data for each case is built on demand, and the platform runs the test once per entry in the data set.

groups.name: Command line test run with JSON output
groups.summary: The whole test suite can be run from the command line. It returns structured JSON with pass, fail and skip counts and a real exit code, so a failed assertion fails the build.

groups.name: Test handlers
groups.summary: Test handlers keep setup and reporting out of the test logic. A handler is specified on the test codeunit and offers hooks before and after the test codeunit run, the test procedure run and each test case run. The demo uses a logger handler that traces while tests run.

groups.name: Default test handlers
groups.summary: A default test handler can be added by extending the default test handlers enum with an implementation, so it covers all test cases that run. It can implement just one hook, such as before test codeunit run, and works next to handlers on a specific test codeunit.

groups.name: Call graph analysis (AL tool graph command)
groups.summary: The AL .NET tool gets a graph command that builds a call graph across an extension and its dependencies. You or a coding agent can query it, for example to find who can call an internal procedure, where the public boundary is, or the path from a page action to a method. It is a static offline analysis, so output can be compared between versions.

groups.name: Launch profiling MCP proxy
groups.summary: A new AL tool command lets a coding agent start, monitor and stop a performance profile and look at the results, with the same kind of tooling and parameters as in Visual Studio Code. The agent needs to know the environment and the profile speed settings.

groups.name: Launch snapshot MCP proxy
groups.summary: A new AL tool command lets agents target a specific environment and tenant and start a snapshot recording while a user is working. It captures values and the call stack to find a bottleneck, an error or another issue, with fewer parameters than the profiling proxy.

groups.name: MCP data tools (find tables, table relations, table schema, data query)
groups.summary: Four new system tools are enabled through the data tool server feature, letting the LLM in an MCP host build AL queries that Business Central compiles and runs, returning the data with no APIs needed. Compile failures return messages straight from the Business Central compiler, so the agent can often correct itself before running the final queries.

groups.name: Server features box in MCP configuration
groups.summary: The MCP configuration page has a new server features box that separates server features, such as the data tool, from the APIs below. Each feature shows which system tools it opens, and enabling several features shows the combined set of tools.

groups.name: MCP server on/off toggle
groups.summary: A new security toggle on the Copilot and agent capabilities page activates or deactivates the MCP server as a whole. This gives full control over whether the feature is available.

groups.name: MCP server landing page (aka.ms/bcmcp)
groups.summary: A landing page at aka.ms/bcmcp explains more about the MCP server for Business Central.
